My boss says leave a gap between every rail. A gap? That's sloppy work.
So he lays his own perfect track in January. No gaps. Rail touching rail.
Then July hits. Steel grows when it heats up. Warm a thirty-nine foot rail by a hundred degrees, and it gets about a third of an inch longer.
With no gaps, that growth has nowhere to go, so the track shoves sideways. Railroaders call it a sun kink.
Okay. So the gaps were the plan.
Those gaps made the old clickety-clack. Modern rails are welded with no gaps. Crews heat or stretch the steel before clamping it, so it's stress-free at about a hundred degrees.
